---
title: "GeoSpatial File Inspector"
date: 2026-09-05
categories: [tool, geometry]
description: "Upload a GeoJSON or a Shapefile and get an instant summary — feature count, geometry type, CRS, bounds, attributes, invalid/empty/duplicate geometries, and a chart per attribute column. Free, runs entirely in your browser: the file never leaves your computer."
page-layout: full
---

Upload a file — `.geojson`, or a shapefile as a single `.zip` or as
`.shp`/`.dbf`/`.shx` selected together — and get an instant summary of
what's actually in it, before you dig into any one check.

::: {.callout-tip}
**Private by design.** Your file is processed entirely in your
browser (Python via WebAssembly) — it's never uploaded to any server,
including ours. Nothing to configure, nothing to trust: the code
never gets the chance to see your data.
:::

```{.webgeods-python #inspect-example-py}
import json

# Deliberately varied, not just geometry-focused: one exact duplicate,
# one invalid (self-intersecting) geometry, one missing numeric value,
# a genuinely low-cardinality categorical column ("zone") and a
# genuinely high-cardinality one ("name", unique per feature) -- so
# every stat AND every column-profile kind (numeric, categorical,
# too-many-distinct-values) has something real to show.
ZONES = ["residential", "commercial", "industrial"]
features = []
for i in range(20):
    col, row = i % 5, i // 5
    x0, y0 = 12.40 + col * 0.05, 41.80 + row * 0.05
    x1, y1 = x0 + 0.04, y0 + 0.04
    population = None if i == 7 else 100 + i * 37
    features.append({
        "type": "Feature",
        "properties": {
            "name": f"parcel-{i + 1}",
            "zone": ZONES[i % 3],
            "population": population
        },
        "geometry": {"type": "Polygon", "coordinates": [[[x0, y0], [x1, y0], [x1, y1], [x0, y1], [x0, y0]]]}
    })

# An exact duplicate of parcel-1 (same coordinates, different name) --
# tests the duplicate-geometry check.
dup = json.loads(json.dumps(features[0]))
dup["properties"]["name"] = "parcel-1-copy"
features.append(dup)

# The same self-intersecting "bowtie" shape this tool's example has
# always used to test geometry validity.
features.append({
    "type": "Feature",
    "properties": {"name": "bowtie (invalid)", "zone": "residential", "population": None},
    "geometry": {"type": "Polygon", "coordinates": [[[12.75, 41.80], [12.85, 41.90], [12.75, 41.90], [12.85, 41.80], [12.75, 41.80]]]}
})

with open("/uploaded.geojson", "w") as f:
    json.dump({"type": "FeatureCollection", "features": features}, f)

"example data written"
```

The code itself isn't shown here — it's a fixed, non-editable summary
using GeoPandas/Shapely underneath; see the
[full article](/posts/geospatial-file-inspection.html) for the actual
code, editable and explained one stat at a time.

```{.webgeods-python #inspect-py}
#| package: geopandas, shapely
import geopandas as gpd
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

gdf = None
for path in ["/uploaded.geojson", "/uploaded.shp", "/vsizip//uploaded.zip"]:
    try:
        gdf = gpd.read_file(path)
        break
    except Exception:
        pass

# CRS is reported in the file's OWN units below (see the full article
# this tool links to) — a bounding box in the hundreds of thousands is
# itself the "something's off" signal, which reprojecting here would
# erase. Only a MISSING CRS gets corrected (assumed WGS84, flagged) —
# there's nothing native to report otherwise.
crs_warning = None
if gdf is not None and gdf.crs is None:
    gdf = gdf.set_crs("EPSG:4326")
    crs_warning = "No CRS found in the file — assuming WGS84 (EPSG:4326)."

# A chart per attribute column, for the side panel -- computed BEFORE
# the fillna("") pass further down (that fillna exists only so a
# missing value survives JSON serialization of the map/download
# features as an empty string, not to change what "missing" means
# here; doing this after it would turn a numeric column's real nulls
# into non-numeric empty strings and break both the numeric check and
# the null count).
#
# A column earns a chart if it's numeric (a distribution is always
# meaningful), or if it's non-numeric with few enough distinct values
# to read as genuinely categorical (zoning, road type, status) rather
# than a near-unique identifier (name, id) where a bar per value would
# say nothing. MAX_CATEGORIES is the one knob for that line.
MAX_CATEGORIES = 15

column_profiles = []
if gdf is not None:
    for col in [c for c in gdf.columns if c != "geometry"]:
        series = gdf[col]
        non_null = series.dropna()
        null_count = int(series.isna().sum())

        if len(non_null) == 0:
            column_profiles.append({"name": col, "kind": "empty"})
            continue

        if pd.api.types.is_numeric_dtype(series):
            values = non_null.to_numpy(dtype=float)
            distinct_values = len(set(values))
            counts, edges = np.histogram(values, bins=min(10, max(1, distinct_values)))
            column_profiles.append({
                "name": col,
                "kind": "numeric",
                "binEdges": [round(float(e), 4) for e in edges],
                "counts": [int(c) for c in counts],
                "nullCount": null_count
            })
            continue

        value_counts = non_null.astype(str).value_counts()
        if len(value_counts) <= 1:
            column_profiles.append({
                "name": col, "kind": "constant",
                "value": str(value_counts.index[0]) if len(value_counts) == 1 else None
            })
        elif len(value_counts) > MAX_CATEGORIES:
            column_profiles.append({
                "name": col, "kind": "highCardinality",
                "distinctCount": int(len(value_counts))
            })
        else:
            column_profiles.append({
                "name": col,
                "kind": "categorical",
                "categories": value_counts.index.tolist(),
                "counts": [int(c) for c in value_counts.to_numpy()],
                "nullCount": null_count
            })

if gdf is not None:
    if "name" not in gdf.columns:
        gdf["name"] = [f"geometry {i+1}" for i in range(len(gdf))]

    # Three per-feature checks, each cheap and vectorized (no O(n²)
    # pairwise comparisons — unlike topology-checker.qmd's check_gap()/
    # check_overlap(), this tool's whole point is a fast first look at
    # a potentially large file, not an authoritative topology report;
    # that's what the Topology Checker is for, linked below).
    gdf["valid"] = gdf.geometry.apply(lambda g: g is not None and g.is_valid)
    gdf["empty"] = gdf.geometry.apply(lambda g: g is None or g.is_empty)
    # Exact-match only (same WKB bytes) — catches a copy-pasted row,
    # not a topologically-identical polygon traced with different
    # vertex order. That distinction is deliberate: an exact-duplicate
    # check is O(n) via hashing and scales to a large file; a
    # topological one is the O(n²) check the Topology Checker already
    # does, cross-linked instead of duplicated here.
    gdf["duplicate"] = gdf.geometry.to_wkb().duplicated()

    # Keep every original column, fillna("") so a None doesn't
    # silently vanish once this result is serialized to JSON, instead
    # of showing up as an empty value.
    for col in gdf.columns:
        if col != "geometry":
            gdf[col] = gdf[col].fillna("")

attribute_columns = [c for c in gdf.columns if c not in ("geometry", "valid", "empty", "duplicate")] if gdf is not None else []
geometry_types = sorted(set(gdf.geometry.geom_type)) if gdf is not None and len(gdf) > 0 else []
bounds = [round(float(b), 6) for b in gdf.total_bounds] if gdf is not None and len(gdf) > 0 else None
crs = gdf.crs.to_string() if gdf is not None and gdf.crs is not None else None

# MapLibre/GeoJSON require WGS84 — the summary above stays in the
# file's own native CRS on purpose (see comment above), so the map
# gets its own throwaway reprojected copy instead of reusing gdf
# directly. gdf.crs is never None here (a missing CRS was already
# assumed WGS84 above), so this only reprojects when the file actually
# declared something else — and the download button (further down)
# reads "features" (native CRS), not this one.
map_gdf = gdf if (gdf is None or gdf.crs == "EPSG:4326") else gdf.to_crs("EPSG:4326")

{
    "features": gdf.__geo_interface__ if gdf is not None else {"type": "FeatureCollection", "features": []},
    "mapFeatures": map_gdf.__geo_interface__ if map_gdf is not None else {"type": "FeatureCollection", "features": []},
    "columnProfiles": column_profiles,
    "summary": {
        "total": len(gdf) if gdf is not None else 0,
        "geometryTypes": geometry_types,
        "crs": crs,
        "crsWarning": crs_warning,
        "bounds": bounds,
        "attributeNames": attribute_columns,
        "invalid": int((~gdf["valid"]).sum()) if gdf is not None else 0,
        "empty": int(gdf["empty"].sum()) if gdf is not None else 0,
        "duplicates": int(gdf["duplicate"].sum()) if gdf is not None else 0
    }
}
```

```{.webgeods-python #inspect-export-shp-py}
# Only run on demand (see the download button below), not on every
# inspect: re-exports gdf (already in the file's own native CRS, see
# inspect-py's own comments -- no reprojection needed) as an actual
# shapefile (geopandas.to_file()), zips the resulting
# .shp/.shx/.dbf/.prj/.cpg in memory, and returns it base64-encoded --
# same pattern as geojson-shapefile-validator.qmd's
# geometry-export-shp-py.
import base64
import io
import os
import zipfile

gdf.to_file("/tmp/webgeods_export.shp", driver="ESRI Shapefile")

buf = io.BytesIO()
with zipfile.ZipFile(buf, "w", zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED) as z:
    for fname in sorted(os.listdir("/tmp")):
        if fname.startswith("webgeods_export."):
            with open(f"/tmp/{fname}", "rb") as f:
                z.writestr(fname.replace("webgeods_export", "result"), f.read())

base64.b64encode(buf.getvalue()).decode("ascii")
```

*First run loads the Python engine — expect about a minute. Instant
after that, and again each time you come back to this page.*

<div id="gfi-dashboard"></div>

<!-- Page-local, not site-wide -- same reasoning as spatial-classifier.qmd's
     own comment: only this tool's per-column chart needs the ~828KB
     vega bundle among the Vector Toolkit tools. -->
<script src="/vega.min.js"></script>
<script src="/vega-lite.min.js"></script>
<script src="/vega-embed.min.js"></script>
<script src="/vega-chart.js"></script>

<script>
document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", () => {

  // Keeps every chart label short and bounded regardless of the
  // uploaded data's own category names or bin edges -- the full
  // value still reaches the reader via the chart's own tooltip.
  const truncateLabel = (text, max = 12) => {
    const str = String(text);
    return str.length > max ? `${str.slice(0, max - 1)}…` : str;
  };

  // Same coloring convention as geojson-shapefile-validator.qmd's
  // VALIDITY_PAINT — green valid, red invalid — so a reader who has
  // already seen that tool recognizes the color language immediately.
  const INSPECT_PAINT = {
    "fill-color": ["case", ["==", ["get", "valid"], true], "#2ea44f", "#e05252"],
    "fill-opacity": 0.55
  };

  // Line companion to INSPECT_PAINT -- a self-intersecting polygon
  // (this tool's own "bowtie" example) tessellates to a ZERO-area
  // fill in MapLibre, so its fill color alone would never be visible.
  // WebGeoDS.toOutlineFeatures() (shared/ui.js) draws every feature's
  // ring as a line too, which has no such dependency.
  const INSPECT_OUTLINE_PAINT = {
    "line-color": ["case", ["==", ["get", "valid"], true], "#2ea44f", "#e05252"],
    "line-width": 2.5
  };

  new WebGeoDS.Dashboard({
    tool: "geospatial-file-inspector",
    mount: "#gfi-dashboard",
    layout: {
      sidePanel: {
        id: "gfi-column-chart",
        flex: "1 1 320px",
        minWidth: "280px",
        placeholder: "A chart per attribute column appears here after you upload a file or load the example."
      }
    },
    upload: { languages: ["python"], kind: "vector", label: "📁 Upload" },
    example: {
      cellId: "inspect-example-py",
      kind: "geojson",
      status: "✓ example data loaded — browse a chart per attribute column in the side panel."
    },
    emptyStats: [
      ["Features", "0"],
      ["—", "Upload a file or load the example above"]
    ],
    // No `compute` block at all -- this tool has no separate action
    // for the user to configure and run: it's pure, automatic
    // inspection, upload/example straight to a result. That's exactly
    // the gap `inspect.onResult` below fills in Dashboard itself (see
    // shared/dashboard.js's own doc comment on it): every other
    // sidePanel tool on this site populates it from a compute step
    // this one simply doesn't have.
    inspect: {
      cellId: "inspect-py",
      layers: [
        { source: "inspect-py", from: (v) => v.mapFeatures, type: "fill", paint: () => INSPECT_PAINT, fit: true },
        { source: "inspect-py-outline", from: (v) => WebGeoDS.toOutlineFeatures(v.mapFeatures), type: "line", paint: () => INSPECT_OUTLINE_PAINT }
      ],
      stats: (v) => {
        const s = v.summary;
        if (!s || s.total === 0) {
          return [["Features", "0"], ["—", "Upload a file or load the example above"]];
        }
        const geometryLabel = s.geometryTypes.length > 1
          ? `Mixed (${s.geometryTypes.join(", ")})`
          : (s.geometryTypes[0] ?? "—");
        return [
          ["Features", s.total.toLocaleString()],
          ["Geometry", geometryLabel],
          ["CRS", s.crsWarning ? `${s.crs} ⚠️ ${s.crsWarning}` : (s.crs ?? "Unknown")],
          ["Bounds", s.bounds ? s.bounds.join(", ") : "—"],
          ["Attributes", `${s.attributeNames.length}${s.attributeNames.length > 0 ? ` (${s.attributeNames.join(", ")})` : ""}`],
          ["Invalid", String(s.invalid)],
          ["Empty", String(s.empty)],
          ["Duplicates", String(s.duplicates)]
        ];
      },
      legend: (v) => (v.summary && v.summary.total > 0)
        ? [{ color: "#2ea44f", label: "Valid" }, { color: "#e05252", label: "Invalid" }]
        : null,
      // Downloads the enriched GeoJSON (original columns + valid/
      // empty/duplicate) in the file's own native CRS -- v.features,
      // not the map source: the map source holds the WGS84 copy
      // reprojected just for display, and a downloaded file should
      // give back the same CRS it came in. When the upload was itself
      // a shapefile, `shapefile` re-exports one instead. Lives under
      // `inspect`, not `compute` -- this tool has no compute step at
      // all, pure automatic inspection, so its download is ready the
      // moment a file resolves, same as its stats/legend/map already
      // are.
      download: {
        getFeatures: (v) => v?.features,
        filenameSuffix: "-inspected.geojson",
        defaultFilename: "inspected.geojson",
        enabled: (v) => !!(v && v.summary && v.summary.total > 0),
        shapefile: {
          cellId: "inspect-export-shp-py",
          filenameSuffix: "-inspected.zip",
          defaultFilename: "inspected-shapefile.zip"
        }
      },
      onResult: (v) => {

        if (!v || !v.summary || v.summary.total === 0) {
          return;
        }

        const dashboard =
          WebGeoDS.Dashboard.find("geospatial-file-inspector");

        const profiles = v.columnProfiles || [];

        if (profiles.length === 0) {
          return;
        }

        const chartMount = document.createElement("div");
        dashboard.sidePanelEl.replaceChildren(chartMount);

        // One combined dataset, every column's rows tagged with their
        // own column name -- lets a SINGLE Vega-Lite spec do the whole
        // job (data + the dropdown itself + the switch between them),
        // instead of a hand-rolled HTML <select> re-rendering a fresh
        // spec on every change (this tool's first cut, replaced after
        // asking: a chart-embedded control is one more UI language on
        // the page than a webgeods-panel-status <select> would be, but
        // keeps every bit of the interaction declarative in the spec
        // itself, which is what was actually asked for here). Numeric
        // and categorical columns already reduce to the same
        // {bin, binFull, count, order} row shape; a column with no
        // chart at all (too many distinct values, constant, empty)
        // gets one "note" row instead of "bar" rows, rendered by a
        // second, text-mark layer -- see the two `transform`s below.
        const allRows = [];

        profiles.forEach((profile) => {

          const col = profile.name;

          if (profile.kind === "empty") {
            allRows.push({ column: col, type: "note", message: "No data in this column." });
            return;
          }
          if (profile.kind === "constant") {
            allRows.push({ column: col, type: "note", message: `Every value is "${profile.value}".` });
            return;
          }
          if (profile.kind === "highCardinality") {
            allRows.push({ column: col, type: "note", message: `${profile.distinctCount} distinct values — too many for a readable chart.` });
            return;
          }

          const isNumeric =
            profile.kind === "numeric";

          // binFull/category kept alongside the truncated label (bin)
          // so the tooltip still shows the real value even when the
          // on-chart label itself is shortened. `key` is namespaced by
          // column (not just index) since every column's rows now
          // share one dataset/one selection param.
          const rows =
            isNumeric
              ? profile.counts.map((count, j) => {
                  const full = `${profile.binEdges[j].toLocaleString()}–${profile.binEdges[j + 1].toLocaleString()}`;
                  const short = `${profile.binEdges[j].toLocaleString(undefined, { maximumFractionDigits: 0 })}–${profile.binEdges[j + 1].toLocaleString(undefined, { maximumFractionDigits: 0 })}`;
                  return { column: col, type: "bar", bin: truncateLabel(short), binFull: full, count, order: j, key: `${col}::bin-${j}` };
                })
              : profile.categories.map((category, j) => ({
                  column: col, type: "bar", bin: truncateLabel(category), binFull: category, count: profile.counts[j], order: j, key: `${col}::cat-${j}`
                }));

          allRows.push(...rows);

        });

        // Forces an immediate layout pass before measuring below -- a
        // container measured right after insertion, with no yield to
        // the event loop yet, can otherwise read a stale pre-layout
        // width (same fix as kriging-interpolator.qmd's own
        // chart-width bug, found live from a screenshot: the chart's
        // plot area overflowed its own container to the right).
        void chartMount.offsetHeight;

        // AXIS_PAD reserves room for the y-axis's own bin/category
        // labels (left) and the x-axis's ticks/title (bottom) as an
        // EXPLICIT, fixed pixel budget -- not Vega-Lite's own
        // automatic "pad" autosize, which measures label text and
        // adds margin for it. That auto-measurement runs ONCE, at
        // first render: found live, switching this dropdown (bound
        // straight into the spec, see "gfiColumn" below) from a
        // no-chart column (nothing to measure, ~0 margin reserved) to
        // a real histogram clipped every bin label clean off the left
        // edge -- Vega never re-measures margins on a later reactive
        // param change, only on the very first layout. A constant
        // budget generous enough for the longest label this chart can
        // ever show (truncateLabel caps every label at 12 characters)
        // sidesteps that entirely: it's already correct before any
        // data exists to measure.
        const AXIS_PAD =
          { left: 90, top: 6, right: 10, bottom: 34 };

        const chartWidth =
          Math.max(80, chartMount.getBoundingClientRect().width - AXIS_PAD.left - AXIS_PAD.right);

        // Set once from the WIDEST column across the whole file, not
        // recomputed per selection -- a single spec's "height" isn't
        // reactive to which column the bound dropdown currently shows,
        // so this sizes for the busiest case (up to 10 numeric bins,
        // or up to MAX_CATEGORIES categories) once, up front.
        const maxRows =
          Math.max(1, ...profiles.map((p) => {
            if (p.kind === "numeric") return p.counts.length;
            if (p.kind === "categorical") return p.categories.length;
            return 1;
          }));
        const chartHeight =
          Math.max(140, maxRows * 26);

        // Reads --etichetta LIVE off :root, same reasoning as
        // shared/vega-chart.js's own designToken() (not imported here
        // -- this page-local script has no dependency on that file's
        // internals): a literal hex baked in here could independently
        // drift from shared/styles.css's own muted-text token.
        const noteColor =
          getComputedStyle(document.documentElement).getPropertyValue("--etichetta").trim() || "#766851";

        WebGeoDS.renderVegaChart(chartMount, {
          "$schema": "https://vega.github.io/schema/vega-lite/v5.json",
          "width": chartWidth,
          "height": chartHeight,
          // "none" -- not "pad" -- pairs with the explicit AXIS_PAD
          // above: total canvas size becomes exactly width/height plus
          // this fixed padding, never recomputed from rendered label
          // text (see AXIS_PAD's own comment for why that recompute
          // never happening is exactly the bug this avoids).
          "autosize": { "type": "none" },
          "padding": AXIS_PAD,
          "data": { "values": allRows },
          "params": [
            // The dropdown itself, bound straight into the spec --
            // Vega-Lite renders this as an actual <select> under the
            // chart (vega-embed's own default "bindings" placement).
            // No onchange handler anywhere in this file: every layer
            // below re-filters against this one signal automatically
            // whenever it changes.
            {
              "name": "gfiColumn",
              "value": profiles[0].name,
              "bind": { "input": "select", "options": profiles.map((p) => p.name), "name": "Column  " }
            },
            { "name": "gfiColumnExternal", "value": null }
          ],
          "layer": [
            {
              "transform": [{ "filter": "datum.column === gfiColumn && datum.type === 'bar'" }],
              "params": [{ "name": "gfiColumnSelect", "select": { "type": "point", "fields": ["key"] } }],
              "mark": { "type": "bar", "color": "#42583c" },
              "encoding": {
                // Horizontal bars: the bin/category label reads
                // left-to-right at a normal angle instead of being
                // squeezed and tilted under the axis -- the actual
                // readability fix. No axis title on this side either
                // (the dropdown above already names the column;
                // repeating "Category"/"Value" rotated beside the bars
                // added nothing).
                "y": { "field": "bin", "type": "nominal", "sort": { "field": "order" }, "title": null, "axis": { "labelFontSize": 10 } },
                "x": { "field": "count", "type": "quantitative", "title": "Count" },
                "tooltip": [{ "field": "binFull", "title": "Value" }, { "field": "count" }]
              }
            },
            {
              // The companion to the bar layer above: a column with no
              // chart (too many distinct values, constant, empty) has
              // no "bar" rows to filter to, so this text layer -- the
              // only one with a matching "note" row for that column --
              // is the only thing that actually draws. Centered via
              // signal expressions (Vega-Lite 5's `"value": {"expr"}`)
              // rather than a data-driven x/y, since a note has no
              // natural position of its own the way a bar does.
              "transform": [{ "filter": "datum.column === gfiColumn && datum.type === 'note'" }],
              "mark": { "type": "text", "align": "center", "baseline": "middle", "fontSize": 12, "color": noteColor, "limit": Math.max(80, chartWidth - 20) },
              "encoding": {
                "x": { "value": { "expr": "width / 2" } },
                "y": { "value": { "expr": "height / 2" } },
                "text": { "field": "message" }
              }
            }
          ]
        }, {
          selectParams: ["gfiColumnSelect"],
          externalParam: "gfiColumnExternal",
          keyField: "key",
          onSelect: () => {}
        });

      }
    }
  });

});
</script>
